title: Valuation differences for coloured binary partitions: the full Ulas–Żmija Conjecture 6.1 picture (even formula, odd bounds, sharpness, and failure of per-colour sharpness for m ≡ 15 mod 16)
exact_endpoint: Ulas.Final5.full_theorem_E2 : EvenFormula ∧ OddOneBound ∧ OddThreeBound ∧ OddOneEquality ∧ OddThreeEquality ∧ FifteenBound ∧ NeverFifteen; Ulas.Final5.mathdb_342364 : ¬ Conj61 (per-k reading P1); Ulas.Final5.conj61_some : Conj61Some (some-k reading P2); all hypothesis-free
scope: Ulas and Żmija, arXiv:1904.03398v1 (Ramanujan J. 55 (2021) 623–660), Conjecture 6.1 on ν2(c_m(4n) − c_m(n)) for m-coloured binary partitions. Proved in full: the even formula ν2 = ν2(n) + 2ν2(k) + 3 for m = 2k; the bounds +3 (m ≡ 1 mod 4) and +6 (m ≡ 3 mod 4) with nonzero differences; explicit infinite equality families for m ≡ 1 (mod 4) and m ≡ 3, 7, 11 (mod 16); and for m ≡ 15 (mod 16) the universal +7 bound, so equality never holds. Hence the conjecture is false under the per-k reading and true under the some-k reading.

substantive_reason: Before this work the even equality and both odd lower bounds were open for every m ≥ 2 (the source had numerics for m ≤ 10, n ≤ 10^5; only m = 1 was classical, by Churchhouse, Rødseth and Gupta). The proof is a new argument: an integral Chebyshev/Pell reduced operator for the even-section transfer (Lemma R), a bit-length weight adapted to halving (Lemma W), Kummer-type even initialization and exact low-coefficient odd initialization. It also shows that per-colour sharpness fails on the infinite family m ≡ 15 (mod 16).
